$comment: Action -> KeyboardEvent.code bindings, applied with input.mapAction by MatchDirector (T-2.26). TWO PLAYERS SHARE ONE KEYBOARD (T-6.6): player 1 has the WASD cluster with E for the weapon, player 2 has the numpad. The two sets never overlap. Bindings are by `code` (physical key), not `key`, so the numpad works whether or not NumLock is on — with NumLock off the numpad still reports Numpad8/4/5/6 as its code even though its `key` becomes ArrowUp/Home/etc. Gamepad is NOT here: the engine's input layer exposes only keysHeld/keysPressed/keysReleased/mouse and has no gamepad channel at all, so pad support is engine work rather than game work.
$weaponNote: Weapon is a TOGGLE, not a hold (2026-08-25). Press once to bring the weapon up, press again to drop it. A spinner takes real time to reach speed, so holding a key for the whole match was both tiring and pointless; and letting go to reposition meant spinning down and paying the spin-up again. WeaponController reads this with input.actionPressed (edge) rather than actionHeld (level).
$player1Note: Weapon moved from Space to KeyE (2026-08-25). Space is now unbound and free. Arrow keys were removed from player 1's drive and turn earlier — they were duplicate bindings for single-player convenience and they now belong to nobody, since player 2 is on the numpad.
$player2Note: Prefixed `p2.` rather than living in a parallel action namespace: actions are a flat registry, so the prefix is what keeps the two players' bindings from colliding. BotDrive picks its prefix from `params.playerIndex`, and WeaponController from `params.action`, which BotAssembler resolves per role — before that fix both bots' weapons read player 1's action and fired together off one key. Numpad layout is the familiar 8/4/6 with 5 as reverse, so the four movement keys sit under the fingers as a block.
